Subject: KMS connectivity & least-privilege routing for PrivNet

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our security engineering team asked for a compact plan that shows how your private deployment will:
- present per-tenant KMS endpoints (BYOK) inside a VPC
- route operator/admin traffic to an HSM cluster without exposing long-lived operator creds
- allow safe key rotation without full tenant downtime

Can you share a short design or checklist we can use in our procurement review? Ideally something showing credential slicing (ephemeral wrapping keys per service) and the network controls we should expect on cross-account peering.

We have a couple of constraints: all control-plane calls must originate from our management subnet (10.8.0.0/24) and any operator sessions must be MFA-bound through our bastion (bastion.edgecloudops.net).

If you can attach a diagram and a short rollout plan, that would be perfect.

Thanks,

Jared — thanks, attaching a concise draft and a diagram. High level summary below; document attached (privnet-kms-draft.pdf).

Summary of approach:
- BYOK key custody: customer uploads root key material to a sealed HSM tenant; we store only wrapped KEKs, not raw key material.
- Credential-slicing: each runtime service receives a short-lived wrapping key (ephemeral KEK) derived from the tenant KEK + service nonce. Ephemeral KEKs rotate on a short cadence (hours) and are issued via a signed assertion from the control plane.
- Network model: control-plane -> customer VPC peering (restricted CIDR), control-plane only allowed from management CIDR (you can provide this), HSM cluster sits in a dedicated subnet with strict SGs and NACLs.
- Operator access: operator sessions must hop through customer-managed bastion and be MFA enforced; operator sessions use ephemeral SSH certs and ephemeral HSM admin tokens which are short-lived and auditable.
- Rotation: tenant KEK rotation performed with a staged rewrap: new KEK is provisioned into HSM, runtime services fetch rewrap tokens and re-encrypt cached secrets without stopping the runtime. Full fallback to previous KEK for 48 hours.

Open questions (please confirm):
1) You mentioned all control-plane calls must originate from 10.8.0.0/24 — can you provide a secondary CIDR for disaster failover?
2) Do you need HSM attestation bundles (TPM/quote) shipped as part of onboarding?

Next steps: Mina and Soojin will sync with you tomorrow to walk the diagram and call out firewall rules to include in your procurement SOW.

Attachments: privnet-kms-draft.pdf, credential-slice-diagram.v1.png

Cheers,
--
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Adding a few ops-level callouts to the draft before we share with EdgeCloudOps security: 

- Ensure the rewrap protocol includes a two-phase commit: runtime acknowledges successful rewrap of cached secrets before we mark old KEK retired. This avoids split-brain where some shards use old KEK and others new.
- Short-lived certificates for the control-plane: we should issue mTLS certs to runtime nodes with expiration <= 1 hour; control-plane rotates CA certs with overlap windows to avoid mass restart.
- Audit stream: HSM operation logs (wrap/unwrap) must be exported to a read-only collector endpoint in the customer VPC; redwood writes signed bundles with per-operation nonces. Provide sample retention policy (30/90/365 days) in the doc.

I'll bring an updated xlsx (access matrix) in the call — it lists which services need KEK unwrap rights vs wrap-only. Olga, can you validate network ACL recommendations for the HSM subnet?

-Mina

Jared / team — quick technical notes ahead of our sync today. Inline below.

> all control-plane calls must originate from our management subnet (10.8.0.0/24)
We will enforce that via a combination of:
- Customer-supplied source CIDR allowlist on the HSM management listener
- mTLS where the client cert is only minted by your bastion's CA (we can validate CRL/OCSP).

> operator sessions must be MFA-bound through our bastion
Operator IAM: we recommend short-lived HSM admin tokens issued after OIDC authentication and Authenticator challenge; tokens carry an aud claim bound to the bastion session id.

> rotation without downtime
Two more details:
1) Ephemeral KEKs are derived deterministically (KDF) from tenant KEK + service-id + epoch. That means services can compute next-tier KEK locally as long as they hold the rewrap token; reduces round-trips.
2) For services that cannot tolerate even short stalls, we'll use background rewrap with cache pre-warming and traffic shifting at the router layer.

Attaching sample access matrix (acme-runtime-access-matrix.xlsx) and a quick diagram. We'll cover port & SG numbers in the call.

Regards,
--
Soojin Lee
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
